analysis:
The only change in docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md is a new 'The cluster waitlist' section (head lines 49-73), a documentation-only change that does not modify code or security controls. The supplied units (head lines 458-1319) are unchanged surrounding text, so I treated them as context and reviewed them against the TB-002, TB-007, TB-011, T-041 and A-001/A-008 definitions. They describe cluster approvals, qualification records, local-only serving, encrypted SSD prefix caches and the update flow; none of these statements was changed by the PR.

The new waitlist section says `darkbloom waitlist cluster` sends only the account to the waitlist and nothing about the Macs. It also says already-paired Macs are never asked and keep working. This describes a client-side or coordinator-side gate that is not visible in the supplied evidence. I could not check the claim that nothing about the Macs is sent, that existing pairs are exempt, or that the waitlist cannot be used as an authorization or entitlement bypass. The waitlist is an approval gating step, not a serving-authorization control, and the existing coordinator approvals, qualification records and App Attest authorization remain authoritative per the docs. Where the waitlist is enforced (CLI only, or coordinator-side) is not visible in this docs-only PR. If the gate is only client-side, it would be a product-policy control and not a security boundary. A later code-bearing pass should check that.

No regression, new attack surface or invalidated threat assumption is shown by the supplied evidence.
